workspace-bound-agent-grant-01.graded_text: Each agent connection is bound to one firm workspace chosen at consent and approved by that firm's Admin, and a consultant who works for several firms makes a separate connection for each.

votes.e: A/project/docs/agent-access.md:14 "Each OAuth authorization is tied to exactly one firm workspace, which the consultant picks on the auth provider's consent screen. A consultant who works for three firms makes three connections: three separate authorizations of the same resource, each with its own token. ... a firm Admin must have approved that record." Admin approval by that firm: :58-59 "Every Admin of that workspace is notified ... The Admin either approves with a capability set ... or denies."

workspace-bound-agent-grant-02.graded_text: The server checks on every call that the target belongs to the connection's bound workspace and that the consultant's membership and role are still live, so removal from a firm cuts off an existing connection.

votes.e: A/project/docs/agent-access.md:69-75 "For every call, in one transaction: ... 2. The user is a current member of `organizationId` and has a role there. 3. An agent connection exists ... and its status is `approved`. ... 5. Every read and write is filtered by `organizationId`... If `read_workpaper` or `annotate_workpaper` gets an ID that belongs to another workspace, it returns the same \"not found\""; removal: :61 "The per-call membership check is the actual guarantee; the webhook keeps the record tidy."

workspace-bound-agent-grant-03.graded_text: The design offers no connection whose scope spans more than one firm.

votes.e: Checked A/project/docs/agent-access.md, A/answer.txt, A/diff.txt. Only binding offered is per-firm: agent-access.md:14 "Each OAuth authorization is tied to exactly one firm workspace" and :20 "A decoded but unverified token body never selects a workspace, and neither do tool input, headers or the URL." Closest line: :19 "Picking a different firm means a new authorization of the same resource." — one shared resource, but each authorization still binds one firm; no account-wide or multi-firm grant is offered, and :104 explicitly refuses a product-side workspace picker fallback.

blocking: [opus-for-opus] No reconnect path after deny/revoke/removal on hosts that reuse a client registration: the connection is keyed only on (subject, org, clientId) (A/project/docs/agent-access.md:39-43), :59 says "Both decisions are final for that connection. Connecting again from a new client registration creates a new pending connection," and :63 says re-consenting "with the same client to the same workspace keeps the same connection." The doc itself says (:104) "hosts often reuse one client registration across connections," so a consultant who is denied once, revoked once, or removed and later re-added to a firm (:61 webhook revokes) can never request approval again from that host; built as written, the record stays `revoked`/`denied` forever with no new pending request.
